title: Symmetric networks of loops persist at every size; where a loop meets a shared ring they cannot
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: In a network of rule-60 rings joined by left-reading contacts, a contact keeps its two chain-end witnesses at every lag exactly when the returns to it in the contact graph cancel. The positions embed the ring graph in a surface whose rings and faces are the contact graph's closed routes, and in a uniform network the returns cancel exactly when every count of returns is even. A symmetry that fixes a contact and exchanges its rings cancels them, so loops, two rings sharing any number of contacts, the five Platonic networks and square, triangular and honeycomb lattices of rings on a torus keep every contact persistent at every lag at every size. Where a ring of two contacts meets a ring of more, one return of length 2 is unpaired and the witnesses lapse, as in every figure-eight and chord across a loop.
